summary: Proved forward direction of neg_bracket_is_vbracket inductive step and n=0 case of neg_partialBracketExist_is_vbracket. Backward directions require VecEA2 endpoint approach.

sorry_inventory.statement: theorem neg_bracket_is_vbracket (backward direction of inductive step: ¬bf.holds → V.holds)
sorry_inventory.assumption: The V from Lemma 5.3 applied to fChainPred satisfies: ¬bf.holds z0 z1 → V.holds z0 z1
sorry_inventory.why_deferred: The F-chain characterization is genuinely one-directional. Forward (bf.holds → orderedPointsExist 1 fChainPred) works via bracket_implies_fChainPred. Backward (orderedPointsExist → bf.holds) fails because: (1) fChainPred does NOT capture beta_0 (first segment type), (2) F-chain Until witnesses may exceed z1 bound, (3) the V constructed from the F-chain is the WRONG V for backward direction (counter-example: bf with beta_0=False has bf.holds=False but orderedPointsExist=True). The correct V construction requires the VecEA2 endpoint approach from Rabinovich p.10.
sorry_inventory.next_dispatch: Implement neg_vecEA2_is_vvecEA2 by induction on n (VecEA2 witness count). The VecEA2 approach places alpha_0 at the endpoint z0, eliminating the universal-over-first-witness problem. Then derive neg_bracket_is_vbracket via VecEA2.fromBracket.

sorry_inventory.statement: theorem neg_partialBracketExist_is_vbracket (backward direction for n >= 1: ¬partial → V.holds)
sorry_inventory.assumption: The V from neg_partialBracketExist_sufficient satisfies backward direction
sorry_inventory.why_deferred: Same root cause as neg_bracket_is_vbracket. The forward direction uses neg_partialBracketExist_sufficient (sorry-free). The backward requires orderedPointsExist 1 fChainPred → bf.partialBracketExist, blocked by missing beta_0.
sorry_inventory.next_dispatch: May be derivable once neg_bracket_is_vbracket is fully proved, or prove directly via VecEA2.

This dispatch proved the forward direction and the n=0 partialBracketExist case, providing partial progress.
